blurb:

At 50 pounds, he's a medium-sized dog with a high activity level, so he's going to need someone who actually wants to go outside. Daily walks, some yard time, a person who shows up for him. That's the deal, and it's a pretty fair one.

The listing doesn't spell out a big backstory for Papas, and sometimes that's fine. He's a solid, healthy dog who's ready to go. Not every dog needs a dramatic origin story. Sometimes you just need a good one.

blurb:
His name is Hypnotic and yes, he looks exactly like that. He's a two-and-a-half-year-old Belgian Malinois mix, 71 pounds, all legs, and according to the shelter, a full-on busy bee. If you know anything about Malinois, that tracks. These dogs need a job, a person, and some real exercise. Hypnotic has the energy, and the people skills to match it. He loves his people. That part is clear.

He's a little cautious around new dogs at first. Not aggressive, just particular. He wants a proper introduction before he decides you're cool, which is honestly a reasonable policy. Once he's comfortable, he does best with dogs who match his energy. He's housebroken, fully vaccinated, heartworm negative, neutered, and microchipped.

His experience with kids isn't known yet, so if that matters for your household, a meet and greet is the right move before committing. He's at Lewisville Animal Services on College Pkwy. Walk in during visiting hours and ask to meet him.

blurb:
Edgar is an 81-pound Great Pyrenees mix who has figured out that the best seat in the house is the one facing the window. The volunteers call it "nature's TV." He calls it a lifestyle. He's nearly five years old, housebroken, good with other dogs, good with kids, and operates at a pace that could generously be described as unhurried. This is not a dog who needs a 5am run. This is a dog who wants to watch the neighborhood with you and take life one couch cushion at a time.

For a big dog, he brings pretty low drama. Moderate-low activity level means he's not going to bounce off your walls, but he's not a lump either. He's fully vaccinated, heartworm negative, microchipped, and already neutered, so the first vet visit is mostly just introductions.

Edgar is at Lewisville Animal Services in Lewisville, TX. You can walk in during visiting hours or fill out an adoption application online at the link above. For a dog this chill, it's worth the drive.

blurb:
Her name is Thing, she's three months old, and she has already been out there doing it on her own. She came in from outside and she's used to looking out for herself. She's cautious around new people and new situations, which makes complete sense given where she's been. She's not broken. She's just careful.

She's already litter box trained and does fine around other cats, which is a lot for a kitten who started life outside. She'd do best in a quieter home without young kids right now, at least while she's still getting her footing. Give her some space at first and let her set the pace. That's usually all a cat like this needs.

Thing is vaccinated, microchipped, and already spayed. She weighs 3.8 pounds, so she's still tiny. If you've got a calm household and some patience, she's got a lot of room to grow into a genuinely good cat.

blurb:
She's only a year and a half old and already has her whole personality figured out. Bridgette is a sleek, pretty domestic shorthair who loves attention, loves to play, and has a very clear stance on one thing: no being picked up. All four paws stay on the floor, and she'd like you to respect that. Everything else is fair game.

Get down on her level and she'll roll around on her back purring like she's known you for years. She's got real energy for play and will absolutely never say no to catnip. If you're looking for a cat who's going to be interactive and present without being clingy or demanding, Bridgette is worth the drive.

She's litter box trained, vaccinated, microchipped, and already spayed. No compatibility notes on kids or other animals yet, so if that matters for your household, the shelter can walk you through what they know. Walk-ins are welcome during visiting hours.

Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville, Texas.
